title: Nvidia CEO’s Exit Looms
summary: Well, that didn’t take long. Jensen Huang’s time as CEO of Nvidia appears to be coming to an end,according to multiple reportsthat the board was meeting Wednesday night to consider his future. Just three days ago, it announced an inquiry into whether he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” but at the time the board said it had “confidence in Jensen.” It seems likely that confidence was undermined by aNew York Times storyon Wednesday that said Huang had had an affair with a company executive in addition to an industry executive who may also be a Chinese spy.If the board dumps Huang, it will demonstrate that no CEO is indispensable, no matter how vital their role is. Many observers had insisted the opposite in recent days, perhaps understandably. After all, Huang co-founded the company and still owned 3.6% of the stock, making him one of the biggest shareholders. As we wrotein this piece, he “has a hand in nearly every aspect of the company’s day-to-day operations.” Along with Sam Altman, he’s been probably the most articulate advocate for AI. Most importantly, his vision of the future has positioned Nvidia to benefit more than any other company from the AI boom, driving its market capitalization to a high of $5.8 trillion in early October, according to Koyfin.
title_es: Jensen Huang podría dejar la dirección de Nvidia según reportes

El movimiento tendría implicaciones significativas para la industria de IA dada la influencia de Huang en la dirección estratégica de la empresa.
bajada_en: Multiple reports indicate Nvidia's board is considering replacing CEO Jensen Huang following a foreign intelligence inquiry and personal matters. The move would have significant implications for the AI industry given Huang's influence on the company's strategic direction.

title: shadcn /improve
summary:
improve An agent skill that audits any codebase and writes implementation plans for other agents to execute. The idea: use your most capable model for the part where intelligence compounds — understanding the codebase, judging what's worth doing, writing the spec — and hand execution to cheaper models. The skill never implements anything itself. The plan is the product. you          →  /improve                    (expensive model, advises)
plans/       →  001-fix-n-plus-one.md       (self-contained specs)
other agent  →  implements, tests, ships    (cheap model, executes) Install npx skills add shadcn/improve Works in any agent that supports Agent Skills format. The plans it writes are plain markdown, so any agent (or human) can pick them up. Usage /improve                        full audit → prioritized findings → plans
/improve quick                  cheap pass: hotspots, top findings only
/improve deep                   exhaustive: every package, every category
/improve security               focused audit (also: perf, tests, bugs, ...)
/improve branch                 audit only what the current branch changes
/improve next                   feature suggestions — where to take the project
/improve plan <description>     skip the audit, spec one thing
/improve review-plan <file>     critique and tighten an existing plan
/improve execute <plan>         dispatch a cheaper executor, review its work
/improve reconcile              refresh the backlog: verify, unblock, retire
/improve ... --issues           also publish plans as GitHub issues How to use A typical first run, start to finish: Open your agent in the repo and run /improve (or /improve quick to keep it cheap). It maps the repo, audits it, and comes back with a findings table. Reply with the ones you want planned — "plan 1, 3 and 5". title: vercel-labs /agent-browser
summary:
agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. Install npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) Homebrew: brew install agent-browser , then agent-browser install . Linux: agent-browser install --with-deps also installs the browser's system libraries. No install: npx agent-browser open example.com . Project installs, building from source, upgrade , and doctor are covered in Installation . Quick start agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close The snapshot for example.com : - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit" . See Selectors . A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the quick start . How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each --session gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without comm

title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
summary:
arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.
title_es: Equipos humano-agente auditable para experimentación de rayos X autónoma

bajada_en: Researchers demonstrated human-agent systems for autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments with complete auditability. The work shows how agents can collaborate in experimental science while maintaining traceability and allowing humans to validate key decisions.

title: UMAP 0.6: new initialization, new optimizers and faster performance [P]
summary: UMAP 0.6 is out!A new initialization, new optimizers, and faster nearest neighbour search make UMAP much faster and far better at large scale. On 3 million arXiv papers it finishes in under 5 minutes, before UMAP 0.5 has even found its nearest neighbours. (race between UMAP0.5 and UMAP 0.6 video)Code:https://github.com/lmcinnes/umapInstall:pip install -U umap-learn(also on conda-forge)SpeedNeighbour search is ~4x faster by making better use of PyNNDescent.Initialization is faster with a new init method.With the new optimizers, the whole run is reproducible with a fixed seed while using every core. A seeded 0.5 run is single-threaded: 52 minutes, 12x longer.QualityJust as important as how quickly we get a result is the quality of the result. UMAP 0.6 works far better on million-scale datasets thanks to a new, better initialization and significant improvements in the optimizer. It resolves finer cluster structure in fewer epochs, with much finer-scale detail and better neighbourhood accuracy than UMAP 0.5, despite being faster.(video of a tour of finer details in the arXiv map)Recursive initializationA large part of the improvement comes from a brand-new initialization scheme that initializes UMAP using UMAP itself: it lays out a coarse version of the graph structure, then refines it, in a recursive tower of initializations. (video of the unfolding)The result is a starting point much closer to UMAP's final result than the messy blurs from spectral initialization or PCA, and it is produced faster than either. It lets the optimizer settle (to within 3% of the final layout) in far fewer epochs than older initialization approaches. title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
summary: Nvidia’s cofounder and chief executive resigned on Thursday after the company opened an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
title_es: Colette Kress es la nueva CEO interina de Nvidia
bajada: La CFO de Nvidia, Colette Kress, asume el cargo de CEO interina tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang. Kress ha sido clave en transformar a Nvidia en potencia de IA.
bajada_en: Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress takes interim CEO role following Jensen Huang's resignation. Kress has been instrumental in transforming Nvidia into an AI powerhouse.

title: Nvidia’s Dealmaking Binge Faces a Reckoning After Jensen Huang’s Exit
summary: In the last three years, Nvidia has emerged asone of the most active backersof AI startups, small cloud providers and frontier AI labs—largely thanks to CEO Jensen Huang’s unrelenting focus on ensuring continued, strong demand for its specialized AI chips. With his sudden resignation late Wednesday, that source of cash now looks at risk.Venture capitalists, startup founders and semiconductor executives say they expect Nvidia to pull back on its frenetic dealmaking pace,which totaled $140 billion, including massive credit guarantees, in just two months this year. That activity includes showering cash on big chip users—Nvidia plans to put $10 billion into Anthropic’s initial public offering next week. But the most vulnerable could be the companies in the middle of funding rounds in which Nvidia is expected to invest.
title_es: OpenAI invierte $2M en investigación sobre IA y seguridad infantil
bajada: OpenAI compromete 2 millones de dólares para investigar los riesgos y oportunidades de la IA para menores. El programa busca desarrollar herramientas compartidas para medir el impacto en jóvenes usuarios.
bajada_en: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI safety for children. The program aims to develop shared tools to measure AI's impact on young users.

title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
summary: OpenAI commits $2 million to research on AI and children’s safety. The work supports shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.
title_es: United Airlines bloquea agentes IA en reservas por riesgos de seguridad
bajada: United Airlines prohíbe que clientes utilicen agentes de IA para reservar vuelos por preocupaciones de ciberseguridad. Esta decisión refleja temores crecientes sobre la seguridad de sistemas autónomos en operaciones críticas.
bajada_en: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights citing cybersecurity risks. The decision reflects growing concerns about autonomous system security in critical operations.

title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
summary: Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found. title_es: Más desarrolladores de juegos adoptan IA generativa
bajada: El 40% de desarrolladores de videojuegos usa IA generativa en su trabajo, un aumento del 36% en 2025, según encuesta de GDC. La adopción crece especialmente en herramientas de producción y diseño.
bajada_en: 40% of game developers now use generative AI in their work, up from 36% in 2025, according to GDC survey. Adoption is growing especially in production and design tools.

title: Free Chinese AI Can Hack Companies While Frontier Developers Face Diminishing Returns
summary: Chinese AI that anyone can download for free has become good enough to break into corporate networks, said Ariel Zeitlin, co-founder and chief technology officer of Tenzai, an Israeli startup that sells hacking software for testing corporate defenses, known as continuous penetration testing.At the same time, the most advanced AI that had an early lead in cybersecurity capabilities is getting harder and costlier to improve, said Micah Hill-Smith, CEO of AI benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis. That means Chinese models won’t be far behind and makes it unlikely that any one developer pulls far ahead of its rivals.
title_es: Nectar lanza agente IA para automatizar descubrimiento de influencers
bajada: Nectar presenta un agente IA que automatiza el descubrimiento de creadores y gestión de outreach para marcas. La herramienta integra búsqueda, comunicación y tracking de campañas en una plataforma.
bajada_en: Nectar launches AI agent to automate creator discovery and partnership management for brands. The tool integrates search, outreach, and campaign tracking in one platform.
